objetivos.descripcion: Why this archive exists: to preserve the programmes of the eisteddfodau of Welsh Patagonia, on a not-for-profit, open-source basis.
objetivos.intro: Amgueddfa (Welsh for museum) brings together the programmes of the eisteddfodau of Welsh Patagonia so that they aren't lost and anyone can look at them.
objetivos.preservar_titulo: Preserving the Welsh culture of Patagonia
objetivos.preservar_1: The programmes tell the story of more than a century of competitions, poems, choirs and recitations. Many are scattered across homes, libraries and associations, and some have already been lost.
objetivos.preservar_2: So we gather and look after the ones we find, and the community can fill in what's missing: uploading programmes, transcribing them and adding facts about each eisteddfod.
objetivos.lucro_1: The archive carries no advertising, doesn't sell data and makes no commercial use whatsoever of the documents.
objetivos.lucro_2: The associations remain the owners of their material. Each document is credited to its association, and if an association wants us to correct or remove something, we do.
objetivos.lucro_derechos: How to ask us to correct or remove a document
objetivos.abierto_1: The site's code is open, and anyone can review it, suggest improvements or use it for another archive.
objetivos.licencia_codigo: The code is published under the AGPL-3.0 licence: you can use and modify it, and if you publish a modified version you must share your changes under the same licence.
objetivos.licencia_datos: The transcriptions and facts contributed by the community are published under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence: they can be reused as long as you credit the source and share anything derived from them under the same licence.
objetivos.licencia_imagenes: The images of the programmes are not covered by those licences: they still belong to each association.

derechos.descripcion: How to ask us to correct or remove a document from the archive, and which licence contributions are published under.
derechos.intro: We respect the rights of the associations and of authors. If a document in the archive belongs to you or concerns you and you'd like us to correct or remove it, follow these steps.
derechos.alcance_1: We publish low-resolution images of the programmes for preservation and reference, and each document is credited to its association. We don't sell any document or use it commercially.
derechos.quien_1: The associations that organise the eisteddfodau, the authors or their heirs, whoever holds the rights to a document, and the people who appear in it.
derechos.pedido_1: Write to us at the address shown at the bottom of every page with these details:
derechos.pedido_doc: Which document it is: the link to its page in the archive.
derechos.pedido_caracter: In what capacity you're asking: for example, on behalf of an association, as the author or as the rights holder.
derechos.pedido_motivo: The reason, and whether you'd like us to correct it (and what to change) or remove it.
derechos.plazos_1: We reply within 10 working days. While we look into a request, we hide the document in question.
derechos.contra_titulo: If something you contributed was removed
derechos.contra_1: If we remove material you uploaded and you believe it was a mistake, you can send us a counter-notice at the same address, with the document, why you believe it can be published and your contact details. We'll pass your reply on to whoever made the request and, if the request doesn't stand up, we'll publish the document again.
derechos.ley_1: This procedure follows the notice and counter-notice structure of the DMCA (the United States copyright law), but it is based on Argentine intellectual property law, Law 11.723.
derechos.ley_2: The site is served from GitHub Pages, so you can also send a DMCA notice directly to GitHub.
derechos.aportes_1: By uploading material or sending a contribution, you confirm that you're able to share it: that it's yours, that you have permission, or that it's a document that can be made public.
derechos.aportes_2: The transcriptions and facts you contribute are published under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence. The images of the programmes still belong to each association.

privacidad.descripcion: What personal data the archive keeps, what for, who handles it, and how to ask to see, correct or delete it.
privacidad.intro: We keep the bare minimum needed for you to sign in and contribute. Here we explain what we keep, what for, and how to exercise your rights.
privacidad.responsable_1: Kevin Roberts, who runs the archive.
privacidad.datos_correo: Your email address, to send you the sign-in link or code. It is never published.
privacidad.datos_idioma: The language you use the site in, so we can send your sign-in emails in it. It is not published.
privacidad.datos_nombre: Your public name, which you choose when you sign in and which appears next to your contributions and on the leaderboard.
privacidad.datos_pais: Your country, if you choose to show it. It's public and appears on your profile and on the leaderboard.
privacidad.datos_zona: Your time zone, if you choose one. It's private and only used to show you dates.
privacidad.datos_aportes: Your contributions (images, transcriptions, facts and memories) and the points you earn with them.
privacidad.publico_1: Your public name, your country if you chose to show it, your approved contributions and your points. Your email address and your time zone are never published.
privacidad.conteo_1: We count how many people sign in each hour, without recording who. We also count visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics, without cookies and without identifying you.
privacidad.proveedores_1: We use these services to run the archive:
privacidad.prov_cloudflare: Cloudflare: stores the archive's images (R2) and counts visits (Web Analytics).
privacidad.prov_correo: The sign-in email is sent by Supabase or, once the archive uses its own email provider, by that provider (Resend).
privacidad.conservacion_1: We keep your data for as long as you have an account. If you ask us to delete it, we delete your email address, your name and your profile.
privacidad.derechos_1: Under Argentina's Personal Data Protection Law 25.326, you can ask to see your data, correct it or delete it. Write to us from your account's email address to the address shown at the bottom of every page.
privacidad.derechos_plazos: We'll show you your data within 10 calendar days, and correct or delete it within 5 working days.
privacidad.derechos_aportes: If you ask us to delete your account, contributions that have already been published stay in the archive under the CC BY-SA 4.0 licence, under your name or anonymously, as you prefer.
privacidad.derechos_aaip: If we don't reply, you can complain to the Agencia de Acceso a la Información Pública (Argentina's Agency for Access to Public Information), which oversees compliance with that law.

accesibilidad.descripcion: How we make the archive usable by everyone: reading settings, the standards we follow, what is still missing and how to tell us about a barrier.
accesibilidad.intro: We want everyone to be able to use the archive, including people who are blind or partially sighted, Deaf or hard of hearing, have limited mobility, or find reading or concentrating difficult.
accesibilidad.ajustes_1: They change how the site looks and are saved in this browser. You'll also find them behind the button with two letter As at the top of every page.
accesibilidad.ajustes_navegador: You can also use your browser's or system's own tools: zoom (Ctrl and +, or ⌘ and + on a Mac), high contrast mode, a screen reader or read-aloud. The site follows your system's preferences for more contrast and less motion.
accesibilidad.normas_1: Our aim is to meet Level AA of the W3C's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2, the international standard for web accessibility:
accesibilidad.normas_ley: That also covers what Argentina's web accessibility law, Law 26.653, requires (as set out in ONTI Provision 6/2019, based on WCAG 2.0), and the European standard EN 301 549. As a private archive with no public funding we are not bound by the law, but we follow it anyway:
accesibilidad.normas_aria: Controls use native HTML and follow WAI-ARIA 1.2: every page has headings, landmarks and a skip link, and everything can be used with a keyboard:
accesibilidad.estado_1: The site is partially compliant with WCAG 2.2 Level AA: the site's navigation, forms and text comply, but part of the archive's content does not yet. This is what we know is missing:
accesibilidad.estado_conforme: As of {fecha}, the pages of this site comply with WCAG 2.2 Level AA.
accesibilidad.limite_imagenes: The programme scans are images of historical documents. Each has a short description, but many don't have their full text yet. We are adding it bit by bit with transcriptions from the community, and you can help from
accesibilidad.limite_idioma: Transcriptions mix Welsh and Spanish on the same line, and the Welsh passages are not marked as Welsh, so a screen reader may read them with Spanish pronunciation.
accesibilidad.limite_traducciones: In the translated versions of the site, the titles and text of documents and contributions are shown in their original language and marked as Spanish, even though they are sometimes in Welsh.
accesibilidad.limite_videos: The videos are on YouTube and were published by other people: captions depend on them.
accesibilidad.evaluacion_1: On {fecha} we carried out a self-evaluation: automated tests with axe-core on every type of page and in all seven languages, and checks of contrast, keyboard use, text enlarged to 200%, text spacing and reflow on screens 320 pixels wide.
accesibilidad.evaluacion_2: It has not yet been tested by people who use screen readers or other assistive technologies. If you use one, your feedback would help us enormously.
accesibilidad.tecnologias: The site uses HTML, CSS, WAI-ARIA and JavaScript. Pages can be read without JavaScript; it is needed to sign in and contribute.
accesibilidad.contacto_titulo: If you come across a barrier
accesibilidad.contacto_1: Tell us which page and what happened. We reply within 10 working days and, if we can't fix it straight away, we'll send you the content in another format.
accesibilidad.agentes_1: The site offers WebMCP tools so that browsers with AI assistants can search documents and editions, change language or adjust the reading settings without guessing at the page. The assistant can fill in the contribution forms, but you always confirm the sending.
